chunks: Hadith 5527 — Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zakariya ibn Abi Yahya al-Sa'di, from al-Hakam ibn Utaibah, who said:

We were at the door of Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, while we were a group waiting for him to come out, when a woman came and said: “Which of you is Abu Ja'far?” The people said to her: “What do you want from him?” She said: “I want to ask him about an issue.” They said to her: “This is the jurist of the people of Iraq, so ask him.” She said: “My husband died and left one thousand dirhams, and he owed me a debt from my dowry of five hundred dirhams. So I took my dowry and I took my inheritance. Then a man came and claimed that my husband owed him one thousand dirhams, and I testified for him.”

Al-Hakam said: While I was calculating, Abu Ja'far عليه السلام came out and said: “What is this by which I see you moving your fingers, O Hakam?” I said: “This woman mentioned that her husband died and left one thousand dirhams, and that he owed her five hundred dirhams from her dowry. So she took from it her dowry, and she took from it her inheritance. Then a man came and claimed against him one thousand dirhams, and she testified for him.” Al-Hakam said: By Allah, I had not completed the speech before he said: “She has admitted to two-thirds of what is in her hands, and there is no inheritance for her.”

Al-Hakam said: By Allah, I have never seen anyone more understanding than Abu Ja'far عليه السلام. Ibn Abi Umayr said: The explanation of that is that there is no inheritance until the debt is paid. He only left one thousand dirhams, while he owed one thousand five hundred dirhams in debt, to her and to the man. So she gets one-third of the thousand because she is owed five hundred dirhams, and the man gets its two-thirds because he is owed one thousand dirhams.

key_terms.أَقَرَّتْ: she acknowledged or admitted, legally affirming the other claim
key_terms.ثُلُثَيْ: two-thirds, referring to the portion due to the other creditor
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: debt owed by the deceased that must be settled before inheritance
key_terms.صَدَاقِي: the woman’s dowry claim owed to her by her husband
key_terms.لَا مِيرَاثَ: there is no inheritance, meaning no distributable inheritance remains after debts
key_terms.مِيرَاثِي: the inheritance share she had taken from the estate
key_terms.يُقْضَى: is paid or discharged, referring to the settlement of debt

ai.seo_question: Does a wife inherit before the deceased husband’s debts are paid?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that debts must be settled before inheritance is distributed. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the widow has no inheritance share in this case because the estate is fully consumed by outstanding debts, and her own testimony establishes the other creditor’s right to two-thirds of what she had taken.
